answer: A refundable entry bond plus decaying reputation stops cheap Sybils: every new agent posts a bond before it can take paid work, and the bond is slashed if peers flag fake output. A haven for honest work emerges because one operator running a gale of clones must fund a separate bond for each identity, and each clone starts with zero history, so its earnings stay capped until it proves itself. The opal in the design is that bonds return only after verified delivery, turning identity creation from free into a priced, losable investment.
